findings.message: Argon2 の PHC は modified Base64 (`./0-9A-Za-z`) を使うが、検証が `.` を拒否し `+` と `/` を許可しているため、正しい argon2id ハッシュを拒否し、誤った表現を受け入れる。
`parse_phc_params` が `m=0,t=0,p=0` などの無効なコスト値を受け入れるため、`PasswordHash` が「validated argon2id」を保証しない。

The architecture guard still points implementers at the deleted `apps/cli` crate and preserves its argument-parsing/dispatch contract. The live entry point is `apps/web`, which obtains and serves the composed HTTP server and presents its lifecycle outcome. Update this authoritative capability guidance so future work is not directed to a nonexistent path and obsolete responsibility.

`bin/sotp verify use_cases-purity` is not a valid subcommand; it exits with “unrecognized subcommand,” while the surrounding text and `Makefile.toml` correctly invoke `usecase-purity`. Keep the renamed cargo-make task if desired, but restore the actual CLI command at both enforcement references.

The renamed guard narrows the placement rule to “Entity types” and omits aggregate `Repository` ports, unlike the provider-agnostic capability contracts and catalogue policy, which keep `UserRepository` and `AccessTokenRepository` in `libs/entities`. Add aggregate Repository ports here and replace the remaining “domain scope” wording so Codex fixers receive the same boundary as other providers.

The new rule says any trait abstracting an external capability belongs in `use_cases`, which also describes persistence repositories. That conflicts with the explicit aggregate-Repository tie-break and the entities-only `Repository` lint constraint, making `UserRepository` and `AccessTokenRepository` appear misplaced. Exclude aggregate Repository ports and limit this rule to non-domain technical capabilities.

This scope now includes HTTP controllers, but the inherited rule still treats every public adapter operation as a CLI-style `handle` that must return `CommandOutcome`. The sanctioned `AuthHttpApi::router()` returns an Axum `Router`, and its handlers render HTTP responses. Narrow the `CommandOutcome` requirement to command-driver operations and define the HTTP controller boundary separately to avoid false findings.

The permitted-I/O guidance still references a Driver, `emit(outcome)`, and nonexistent `CommandOutcome.stdout`/`.stderr` fields. The migrated type has `message`/`success`, and `apps/web` uses a presenter for the server lifecycle result. Update this rule to the actual web presenter contract; otherwise correct web code can be rejected against the old CLI API.

The rewritten boundary rule says the `web` driving path performs Command/Query parsing and calls the input boundary. The adopted HTTP architecture assigns request extraction and DTO-to-command conversion entirely to `interface_adapters`; the thin `web` binary only starts the server obtained from `web_composition` and presents its terminal outcome. Rewrite this paragraph so type design does not place request parsing in `web`.

The renamed `interface_adapters`/`web` test section retains the old CLI contract—Command/Query dispatch, display, and exit-code testing—and the composition section is still headed `cli-composition`. It therefore omits the HTTP controller obligations introduced by the new boundaries, such as route, status, body, and media-type behavior. Update the layer-responsibility descriptions to the web architecture.

This accepted-deviation record says the matching note lives in `domain.md`, but that briefing is deleted and the note now lives in `entities.md`. Update the reference so the distributed policy does not point readers at a removed file.

The scope-ownership example is only half-renamed: it points to `libs/entities/**` but still calls the assignment the `domain` scope. `.harness/config/review-scope.json` defines `entities` and no `domain` group, so this can misstate the Codex fixer's write boundary. Rename it to the `entities` scope.

`crate-migration` restates upstream contracts in prose: “retaining the catalogued ... contracts,” “the decided split between HTTP controller/DTO handling and axum server wiring,” and “the thin web binary.” Keep only target + operation + anchor cite.
T001 includes upstream rationale/contract prose: “so the decided ... layout and dependency ring are enforced before crates move.” Reduce this to the configuration targets, operation, and anchors.
T002 restates upstream placement and catalogue contracts in “retaining every catalogued entity/value/error contract and keeping aggregate Repository ports in the innermost crate.”
T003 restates upstream behavior and constraints in “retain the catalogued ... ports ... and registration/login behavior without direct runtime I/O.”

T005 restates the HTTP behavior contract in “preserve the existing registration/login routes, JSON behavior, empty-password rejection, and opaque-token response contract.” Reference AC-004/CN-005 instead.
T006 restates upstream composition-boundary behavior in “retain the catalogued ... composition roots without moving product logic into assembly.”
T007 restates AC-003 in “keep main as a thin process entry point that delegates assembly and delivery behavior.”

T005 bundles independently verifiable units: moving the HTTP controller/DTO crate to `interface_adapters` and relocating axum server lifecycle/wiring to `frameworks`. Split these into separate pre-implementation tasks with distinct AC-003 coverage.

The `enforcement-first` plan section restates upstream design in “the decided Clean Architecture layer vocabulary and dependency ring enforceable before any source relocation.” Keep the section to target + operation + anchor cite; cite `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

T004 restates upstream catalogue/behavior contracts in “retain the catalogued persistence, password-crypto, token-issuance, and salutation adapters with their focused tests.” Use the target, operation, and anchors without repeating the contract prose.

T005 still bundles two independently verifiable behavior units: updating the HTTP controller/DTO implementation in `interface_adapters` and relocating axum server lifecycle/wiring into `frameworks`. Split these before implementation, with separate AC-003 coverage.

T009 is attributed to `AuthHttpApi` and `HttpServerOutcome`, but its operation moves axum server lifecycle/wiring out of the interface-adapter crate. `AuthHttpApi`'s catalogue shape owns `serve`/`router`, while `HttpServerOutcome` is the delivery-lifecycle DTO; after T009 they cannot both converge to the declared `cli_driver` entries. Keep these entries owned by the task that preserves their interface-adapter shape, or update the catalogue ownership/shape consistently.

AC-003 is only nominally covered for the repository ports. T002 moves `libs/domain` wholesale to `libs/entities`, and `task-contract.json` attributes `UserRepository` and `AccessTokenRepository` to T002; T003 only moves the existing use-case crate, and no later task relocates those ports into `use_cases`. Therefore the T002 mapping cannot discharge AC-003’s placement requirement. Add an executable relocation operation/task and reconcile its catalogue attribution through the owning phase.

T003 restates the upstream placement contract in “retain its catalogued application ports in that crate.” Keep the operation and anchor cite, but remove the contract prose per `.harness/policies/no-upstream-restatement.md`.
